deities: Goddess Samaleswari (Samalei Maa), presiding goddess of western Odisha — worshipped as Jagat Janani, Adishakti, Mahalaxmi and Mahasaraswati

history.dynasty: Chauhan dynasty — present stone structure by King Balaram Dev (r. 1540–1560); sanctum rebuilt in present form by his descendant Chhatra Sai Deo
history.summary: The Samaleswari Temple on the banks of the Mahanadi in Sambalpur is the shrine of Goddess Samaleswari (Samalei Maa), the presiding goddess of western Odisha. Tradition holds that Chauhan king Balaram Dev (1540–1560), first of the Chauhan dynasty in Sambalpur, discovered the deity beneath a Semel (silk-cotton) tree, installed her in his new fort, and formalised her as the state's Ishta Devi; the harvest festival of Nuakhai, offered to the goddess as the season's first produce, is credited to his initiation. The present stone structure in Kalinga style — with pyramidal shikhara and garbhagriha — dates to the mid-1500s, with the sanctum rebuilt to its present form a century later by Chhatra Sai Deo (per Wikipedia's Balarama Deva article). Samalei was earlier worshipped by the local tribal population; after Lord Jagannath she is the only deity in Odisha presiding over so vast a region (western Odisha, parts of Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand). Major festivals are Nuakhai and Navaratri. Coordinates are a full-address geocode match for the temple.

name: Samaleswari Temple
town_description: Sambalpur, on the Mahanadi river in western Odisha, is the cultural capital of the region — historically known as Hirakhanda, famed for diamonds exported to Rome in antiquity. The Samaleswari Temple at Bada Bazaar is the city's spiritual nucleus, and the deity Samalei gives the city its identity.

travel.airport: Jharsuguda (Veer Surendra Sai Airport) — nearest airport, about 35–40 km away.
travel.railway: Sambalpur Junction — major railhead with connections across India.
travel.road: The temple at Bada Bazaar is well connected by road within Sambalpur city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Nuakhai (Aug–Sep) and Navaratri (Sep–Oct) are the most vibrant festival times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily worship; exact darshan hours are not published online — verify locally before travel.
